sections.title: Urban Empathy: Educational Encounters in a More-Than-Human World
sections.description: Do you ever wonder what other-than-human animals would have to say to us, what they might even teach us, if we learned how to listen? How might multispecies knowledge sharing reshape the future of education, our relationship with the planet, and the systems that govern it? Grounded in the history of education, eco-feminism, urban environmentalism, and multispecies anthropology, this course examines how novel approaches to teaching and learning in urban environments may benefit from investigation of and interaction with the robust multispecies knowledge networks and valuable nonverbal ways of knowing that surround us in cities such as Philadelphia. This 6-week summer course is structured in two parts: “Part I – Places” runs from week 1 to 3, during which we will read about and visit significant urban sites for human/other-than-human animal interaction (park, home, zoo, lab, and university campus) and explore the entangled ecosystems and interspecies knowledge networks that both struggle and thrive in these spaces. “Part II – Situations” runs from week 4 to 6, and we will turn our focus to particular animals (birds, dogs, rats and mice, monkeys, whales and dolphins, and Homo Sapiens), exploring the epistemological orientations and narratives that shape interspecies relations as well as their respective roles in history, science, education, cultures, and society.
